probeErrors.message: Not running on Windows, so this is the sample PC from fixtures/owner-pc.json.

findings.title: RAM runs at 3600 MT/s, its rated speed
RAM runs in dual channel
findings.detail: Your sticks sit on separate memory channels, which doubles memory bandwidth.

findings.title: BIOS is from 2024-05-20
findings.detail: Riot has asked some players to install a BIOS update released after December 2025 to fix a security flaw. Updates also improve memory stability. Updating resets BIOS settings, so turn XMP back on afterwards.

findings.title: Graphics card uses all its PCIe lanes
Run a benchmark to check the PCIe link under load
findings.detail: Graphics cards slow their link when idle, so Kestrel checks it during a benchmark.

findings.title: All monitors run at their top refresh rate
VALORANT runs on your NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti
Power plan is Balanced
findings.detail: This plan lets the CPU slow down between frames, which hurts 1% lows. Kestrel's own plan arrives in stage 5. Until then, pick High performance in Control Panel → Power Options. If it only lists Balanced (laptops with Modern Standby do that), set Settings → System → Power → Power mode → Best performance instead.

findings.title: VALORANT is on an NVMe SSD (C:)
Nothing heavy is running in the background
Memory Integrity is off
findings.detail: VALORANT works fine like this. Riot can require it on for flagged accounts, and Vanguard's On-Demand mode needs it.

findings.title: IOMMU is off
findings.detail: Only needed for Vanguard's On-Demand mode, or if Riot asks for it. It's called VT-d on Intel and IOMMU or AMD-Vi on AMD.

findings.title: Not eligible for Vanguard On-Demand mode
findings.detail: Missing: VBS, Memory Integrity, IOMMU. On-Demand is optional; VALORANT works without it.

findings.title: Network adapter power saving is on
findings.detail: Windows can let the adapter doze, which causes small latency spikes. Kestrel's Competitive tier turns this off in stage 6.

guide.tip: Press F7 to switch between EZ Mode and Advanced Mode. The Search button at the top finds any setting by name.

sections.title: Turn on XMP
sections.why: Most RAM starts at a safe, slow default speed. XMP runs it at the speed on the box, which can add a lot of FPS in CPU-heavy games like VALORANT.
steps: Restart and press Del to open the BIOS.
Press F7 for Advanced Mode.
Open the Extreme Tweaker tab.
Set Ai Overclock Tuner to XMP I.
Check that DRAM Frequency shows your kit's speed, then press F10 and choose Yes.
sections.caution: If the PC won't start, it usually retries with safe settings by itself. If it doesn't, clear the BIOS settings (Clear CMOS) and try a lower speed.

sections.title: Keep the memory controller in Gear 1
sections.why: On 11th-gen Intel CPUs, Gear 1 runs the memory controller at full speed. Gear 2 adds delay that usually costs more FPS than the extra RAM speed gains.
steps: On the Extreme Tweaker tab, set Memory Controller : DRAM Frequency Ratio to 1:1.
If the PC is unstable at your kit's speed in 1:1, set DRAM Frequency to DDR4-3200 and keep 1:1.
Press F10 and choose Yes.
sections.caution: Crashes or blue screens after this change mean the memory can't hold that speed in Gear 1. Lower the frequency.

sections.title: Update the BIOS
sections.why: Riot has asked some players to install BIOS updates released after December 2025 to fix a security flaw. Updates also improve memory compatibility.
steps: Download the latest BIOS for ROG MAXIMUS XIII HERO from ASUS support and copy it to a USB stick.
In the BIOS, open Tool → ASUS EZ Flash 3 Utility.
Pick the file on the USB stick and confirm.
sections.caution: Don't turn off the PC while it updates. Updating resets BIOS settings, so turn XMP back on afterwards. On 11th-gen Intel the memory gear goes back to its default too, so set Gear 1 again.

sections.title: Run the graphics card at full PCIe speed
sections.why: The card should use all its lanes (usually x16) at the PCIe generation it and the slot support. It drops when it sits in a lower slot, shares lanes with an M.2 drive, or the slot is set to an older generation.
steps: Shut down the PC and check that the graphics card sits in the top long slot (the one closest to the CPU), pushed fully in with the slot's latch closed.
If your board's manual says an M.2 slot shares lanes with the graphics card's slot, move that drive to another M.2 slot.
Start the PC and open the BIOS.
Press F7 for Advanced Mode.
Open Advanced → System Agent (SA) Configuration → PCI Express Configuration.
Set the top x16 slot's link speed (PCIEX16_1 Link Speed or similar) to Auto.
Press F10 and choose Yes.
sections.caution: Menu names vary between boards and BIOS versions. Your board's manual lists which slots and M.2 drives share lanes.

sections.title: Resizable BAR (optional)
sections.why: Lets the CPU reach all of the graphics card's memory at once. VALORANT gains little, but some other games do.
steps: Press F7 for Advanced Mode.
Open Advanced → PCI Subsystem Settings.
Set Above 4G Decoding to Enabled, then Re-Size BAR Support to Auto.
Press F10 and choose Yes.
sections.caution: Windows must start in UEFI mode (CSM off) for this to work.

sections.title: Turn on virtualization (only if you need it)
sections.why: Windows needs it for Memory Integrity, which Riot can require on flagged accounts. It doesn't change FPS.
steps: Press F7 for Advanced Mode.
Open Advanced → CPU Configuration.
Set Intel (VMX) Virtualization Technology to Enabled.
Press F10 and choose Yes.
sections.caution: Menu names vary between boards and BIOS versions. If you can't find it, search the BIOS for SVM or Virtualization.

sections.title: Turn on IOMMU (only if you need it)
sections.why: Vanguard's optional On-Demand mode needs it, and Riot can ask for it on some accounts. It doesn't change FPS.
steps: Press F7 for Advanced Mode.
Open Advanced → System Agent (SA) Configuration.
Set VT-d to Enabled.
Press F10 and choose Yes.
sections.caution: Menu names vary between boards and BIOS versions. If you can't find it, search the BIOS for VT-d or IOMMU.
